case_studies.title: Agentic coding without the cloud: evaluating open-weight large language models on longitudinal data preparation tasks
case_studies.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) and agents are now widely used tools in code development, with data typically sent to third-party cloud-based models. Their adoption in research using personal data is constrained by governance requirements that typically prohibit data transmission to external services. Locally deployable open-weight models offer an alternative since sensitive data never leave the local environment. We introduce an open-source framework for evaluating the efficacy of AI agents powered by open-weight LLMs on one of the most persistent bottlenecks in research on longitudinal populati
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of securely using large language models for code development with sensitive data by building an open-source framework for evaluating locally deployable open-weight models. The result is an alternative to cloud-based models that can keep sensitive data local. This is relevant for organizations with strict data governance requirements.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage infrastructure for research or organizations with sensitive data, here is what to do: consider using locally deployable open-weight large language models, evaluate the open-source framework for your specific use case, and assess the security benefits of keeping data local. This flags a risk: if your org uses cloud-based models for sensitive data, check your data governance policies immediately.
